question: Where was the 13th Governing Council Meeting of the Bay of Bengal Inter-Governmental Organization (BOBP-IGO) held?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Male, Maldives**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **13th Governing Council Meeting** of the Bay of Bengal Inter-Governmental Organization (BOBP-IGO) was held in **Male, Maldives** in 2023.
 
• The meeting focused on sustainable fisheries management and regional cooperation among member countries of the Bay of Bengal region.
 
• BOBP-IGO is an intergovernmental organization that aims to promote responsible fisheries and marine ecosystem conservation in the Bay of Bengal region.
 
• Member countries of the BOBP-IGO include **Bangladesh, India, Maldives, and Sri Lanka**.
 
• The Governing Council Meetings are held annually to discuss and address key issues pertaining to fisheries and marine resource management.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bay of Bengal Programme Inter-Governmental Organization (BOBP-IGO)**

 
 
• Established in 2003, BOBP-IGO works to enhance the socio-economic condition of small-scale fisheries in the Bay of Bengal region.
 
• The organization promotes sustainable fishing practices and capacity-building initiatives for member countries.
 
• Its primary focus is on conserving marine biodiversity while addressing the livelihood challenges faced by coastal communities.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Fisheries Management**
 
 
• Sustainable fisheries aim to balance the ecological, economic, and social aspects of marine resource utilization.
 
• It focuses on maintaining fish stocks at biologically safe levels and reducing overfishing.
 
• Efforts include implementing regulations, promoting aquaculture, and engaging local communities in conservation practices.
 
 
 
• **Regional Cooperation in Fisheries**
 
 
• Regional cooperation is crucial for managing shared marine resources and addressing transboundary challenges like illegal fishing.
 
• Organizations like BOBP-IGO facilitate dialogue and collaboration among member states.
 
• Joint initiatives often include data sharing, capacity building, and harmonized policies for fisheries governance.
 
 
 
• **Marine Biodiversity Conservation**
 
 
• Marine biodiversity conservation is essential for maintaining the health of ocean ecosystems.
 
• It involves protecting endangered species, restoring habitats like coral reefs and mangroves, and reducing pollution.
 
• Global frameworks like the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) guide conservation efforts.
